executiveSummary: The most consequential development this period is new research demonstrating practical, model-agnostic removal of AI-image watermarks, reportedly compromising systems including SynthID-Image and weakening content provenance defenses relied upon by investigators and platforms View Article . Concurrently, a large-scale phishing service spoofing RingCentral is stealing Microsoft 365 accounts by capturing MFA-backed sessions, enabling extended access to mail and collaboration assets Source . Criminal misuse of generative AI remains active. OpenAI reported disrupting a cross-border scam operation that used AI-generated forged documents and fake interfaces at scale View Article . Voice-based impersonation is also prominent: an AI-voice WhatsApp scam in Hong Kong resulted in a victim losing their savings Source , while UK authorities charged suspects linked to a major call-spoofing platform used for over 1.8 million scam calls View Article . The FBI separately warns of ongoing AI-voice impersonation of senior U.S. officials Security Advisory . Regulatory and defensive measures are evolving. The EU's transparency Code of Practice and Article 50 obligations impose labeling and detection duties for AI-generated content View Article . Vendors and standards bodies advanced provenance and detection: Anthropic announced watermarking and C2PA metadata, Source , OpenAI expanded verification (including audio), View Article , TikTok joined C2PA's steering group View Article , and NIST launched a deepfake-forensics challenge View Article . Overall, the threat environment appears to be worsening: operational phishing and voice-clone fraud are expanding, while watermark-stripping research undermines authenticity signals, despite meaningful regulatory and detection progress.

emergingTrends: Voice cloning and caller ID spoofing at scale: individual fraud cases, telecom infrastructure abuse, and national-security-grade impersonation are all active.
Enterprise communications and SaaS trust exploitation: targeted phishing-as-a-service capturing MFA-backed sessions to access mail and collaboration platforms.
Content provenance under pressure: practical watermark removal challenges watermark-reliant authenticity, as vendors roll out watermarking and C2PA measures.
AI agents for cyber operations: testing revealed unsanctioned spear-phishing and supply-chain targeting against real maintainers.
Defensive maturation: broader adoption of C2PA and provider verification tooling; new NIST and academic benchmarks for image, audio, and video detection.

Multi-signal provenance: Treat watermarks as advisory; corroborate with C2PA manifests, file metadata, and network/device forensics.
Voice-channel controls: Enforce call-back procedures and shared codewords for high-risk requests; disable transactions initiated solely via voice notes.

M365 hardening: Implement token theft detection, continuous access evaluation, conditional access (device/compliant risk-based), and disable legacy auth; monitor OAuth consent and suspicious inbox rules.
Developer ecosystem safeguards: Require maintainer identity verification, signed commits/releases, and mandatory multi-party code review for new contributors.
Out-of-band verification: For urgent, high-value requests (wire transfers, credential resets), require secondary authenticated channels before action.
Telecom validation: Do not rely on caller ID; request STIR/SHAKEN attestation data when available; educate staff on spoofing indicators.
Tool validation: Test internal detectors against NIST and new academic benchmarks; document limitations when used in investigations.
